dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How are your travels through Liyue going?

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: Great! The ruins and history are fascinating, as are the local customs.

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: I mean, a lot of local customs are also derived from history. I've learned a lot just from studying them.

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: Take, for example, this particular record of Liyue wedding customs, which was written about in Customs of Liyue: Flower Ball by a scholar from Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: If it interests you, do take it and have a look. It's very fascinating indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: ...How many secrets does Liyue truly hold?

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: This place we are in is called the Guili Assembly. According to Liyue folklore, it was once inhabited by people — in fact, it was rather prosperous.

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: But for various reasons, the whole place was wiped out. All that remains now is the countless ruins scattered across the landscape.

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: Some stories put it down to the conflict between the gods, other people say it was a war between humans. And some sources talk of a sudden, catastrophic natural disaster...

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: Whatever the reason was, ruins are all that remain here now. The only ones who come here are the hilichurls, the Treasure Hoarders...

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: ...And masochistic scholars, like me, who in spite of all the risks just can't resist the idea of how much research value these ruins have to offer.

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: In practice though, scholars like me aren't actually cut out for this kind of field work! I've hardly covered any ground yet, and I already need a rest...

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: The actual ruin-exploring seems more your area of expertise. What do you say, fancy helping me out?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Secrets?

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: Oh, Traveler, it's you. The secrets I'm referring to are a set of inscriptions.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you mean buried treasure?

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: Haha, who knows? It's always possible. Talk of secrets waiting to be uncovered does tend to make one think of buried treasure.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure.

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: Great. Hmm, but I should give you an idea of what to look for... Yes, keep your eyes peeled for stone pillars and stone tablets.

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: Given how ancient these ruins are, any text we can hope to find will be written on stone, not paper.

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: After all, stone is the oldest and most durable medium for written communication.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What am I looking for?

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: Hmm... Text, essentially. Written messages from the past.

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: And if you're looking for text in ruins as ancient as these, that means looking for stone pillars and stone tablets.

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: Stone is the oldest, most durable medium for written communication. All the more so in the domain of the Geo Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: The stones here have borne witness to all of history. I am sure they will not disappoint.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Only if there's treasure...

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: Whatever treasure you find, you can keep. Material wealth isn't what appeals to me.

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: In Liyue there's a saying that goes: "Money belongs to the world outside your head." I'm more interested in acquiring knowledge than money.

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: So while you're hunting for treasure, please also keep your eyes peeled for stone pillars and stone tablets.

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: Given how ancient these ruins are, any knowledge we can hope to find will be most likely be written on stone.

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: Wow, are you a traveler? Have you made any weird and wonderful discoveries recently?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: I am a scholar from Sumeru. My name is Soraya.

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: I know that each of the seven nations in this world have unique and rich cultures, but what fascinates me the most are the legends of the Liyue adepti.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Soraya
dialogues.text: Bye then. If you hear any interesting stories, do share them with me next time we meet.
